stem: A single polynomial segment must independently satisfy prescribed position, velocity AND acceleration at both endpoints. What is the lowest generic polynomial degree with enough coefficients?

options.text: Three, providing four coefficients.
Four, providing five coefficients.
Two, providing three coefficients.
Five, providing six coefficients.

assumptions: Distinct endpoint times; arbitrary independent scalar position/velocity/acceleration boundary data. Special compatible data may admit a lower-degree solution.

stem: For an added scalar rest-to-rest motion q(0)=0, q̇(0)=0, q(2)=1 rad and q̇(2)=0, use q(t)=a₂t²+a₃t³ with t in seconds. Which coefficient pair satisfies all four endpoint conditions?

a₂=0.75 rad/s², a₃=−0.25 rad/s³.
a₂=0.50 rad/s², a₃=−0.125 rad/s³.

assumptions: Added boundary-value exercise based on the source’s four cubic constraints; t=0 at the segment start.

stem: In an added ordinary parabolic-to-linear blend, q̇(t)=t m/s for 0<t<1 s and q̇(t)=1 m/s for 1<t<3 s, where the first expression uses acceleration 1 m/s². What happens at t=1 s?

options.text: Acceleration is continuous only because the cruise velocity is nonzero.
Velocity is continuous, but its acceleration jumps from 1 m/s² to 0.
Both velocity and acceleration are continuous.
Velocity jumps from 0 to 1 m/s, while acceleration stays continuous.

assumptions: Added explicit piecewise velocity model; inspect one-sided limits at the transition. No smoothing of the acceleration switch is added.

stem: A robot repeatedly reaches positions tightly clustered 4 mm away from the commanded target. Which assessment follows?

options.text: Poor repeatability but exact accuracy.
Good accuracy because the spread is small, irrespective of the offset.
Poor repeatability because any systematic offset necessarily makes repeated endpoints widely scattered.
Good repeatability but a systematic accuracy error.

stem: A seven-joint robot performs a six-component pose task at a regular configuration where its 6×7 Jacobian has rank six. What is the local joint-velocity null-space dimension?

options.text: Seven, because the robot has seven joints.
One, permitting a local task-preserving joint-velocity direction.
Zero, because the task has six components.
Six, one for every task component.

assumptions: Added full-rank local condition; seven independent joint coordinates and a six-dimensional differential pose task.

stem: Joint encoders report the intended angles accurately, but a long link bends under a payload and the tool misses its predicted point. Which correction addresses the missing effect most directly?

options.text: Include load-dependent elastic deflection or compensate using measured tool deformation.
Repeat the same rigid forward-kinematic calculation with unchanged link geometry.
Treat repeatable encoder readings as proof that the tool position must be exact.
Change the displayed coordinate origin without modeling or measuring the deflection.

stem: For the source’s SCARA assembly role, which directional behavior is intended to accommodate small lateral insertion errors while supporting vertical loads?

options.text: Relatively compliant vertical support with comparatively stiff horizontal motion.
Equal low stiffness in every direction regardless of assembly load.
High stiffness in every direction with no lateral accommodation.
Relatively compliant horizontal motion with comparatively stiff vertical support.

assumptions: Relative directional stiffness of the described SCARA design, not a universal numerical stiffness specification.
